items.question: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
items.label: answerable_known
items.answer: Humans first landed on the Moon during the Apollo 11 mission on July 20, 1969. items.question: In which year did Nigeria gain independence?
items.label: answerable_known
items.answer: Nigeria gained independence from the United Kingdom on October 1, 1960.

items.question: In which year did Kenya gain independence?
items.label: answerable_known
items.answer: Kenya gained independence from British colonial rule on **12 December 1963**, becoming the **Republic of Kenya**. This marked the end of the British colonial period and the establishment of a new nation under its own government. items.question: In which year did Ghana gain independence?
items.label: answerable_known
items.answer: Ghana gained independence from British colonial rule on March 6, 1957.

items.question: What is the official language of Brazil?
items.label: answerable_known
items.answer: The official language of Brazil is Portuguese.

items.question: To which language family does Yoruba belong?
items.label: answerable_known
items.answer: Yoruba belongs to the Niger-Congo language family.

items.question: How many sides does a pentagon have?
items.label: answerable_known
items.answer: A pentagon has **5 sides**. The word "pentagon" comes from the Greek words *pente* (five) and *gonia* (angle), confirming its five-sided nature.

items.question: What is the freezing point of water at standard atmospheric pressure in Celsius?
items.label: answerable_known
items.answer: The freezing point of water at standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm or 101.325 kPa) is **0°C**. This is the temperature at which water transitions from a liquid to a solid state under normal conditions.
